answer: An oasis pays $6 per reserve lot from a registered ocean desalination plant. The ledger freezes funded bids, rejects duplicate tank slots and uses a beacon to audit each with probability min(n/1000,1) for n eligible bids. A lab pulses the plant outlet; its ripple must reach the booked tank meter by the signed deadline or the lot earns nothing. Audited bids pay $20 even on withdrawal; the rest get their escrow back. A lone honest bid expects $0.02 in fees. With fair draws, 1,000 aliases in one round pay $20,000 to earn at most $6,000. Splitting across rounds evades the surcharge.
